items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Public types and methods are documented. But the long durability predicate `(seqNum == 0 && (totalDurableCommits > 0 || highestDurableSeqNum > 0)) || (seqNum > 0 && ...)` is copied four times with no comment, and the internal structs (durableRecord, durabilityManager fields) have no docs.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: durability.go is 622 lines, over the 500-line cap. worker() is about 95 lines and mixes sync waiting, stats, job retention, waking waiters and callback dispatch. The durability predicate is copy-pasted. TeeEventListener and Open detect the default callback through reflect (isDefaultBatchDurable).

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Close/error latching works and ctx precedence is handled. Problems: unexplained constants (queue 1024, retention 2048, subscriptions 4096); jobBitset seenJobs grows with every job ID, so retention is not bounded; a blocking `m.queue <- rec` runs inside commitWrite; and the apply error overwrites *userErr.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: The API is purely additive and non-sync commits are unchanged. But every Sync commit, even with BatchDurable unset, now allocates a durableRecord and a channel, takes a mutex, and has its WaitGroup Done routed through one worker goroutine that runs after the user callback. That serializes the commit-ack latency.
